nodes.title: Order and Degree of Differential Equations
points: Differential Equation: An equation involving an independent variable, dependent variable, and derivatives of dependent variable.
Order: The order of the HIGHEST ORDER DERIVATIVE occurring in the differential equation.
Degree: The power (exponent) of the highest order derivative, AFTER the equation is expressed as a polynomial in derivatives (free from radicals and fractions of derivatives).
Degree NOT Defined Trap: If derivatives are inside transcendental functions (e.g., e^(dy/dx), sin(dy/dx), ln(dy/dx)), the degree is NOT DEFINED, though order is still defined.

formulas.label: Degree
formulas.expr: Degree = Power of highest derivative (polynomial form)

nodes.title: Formation of Differential Equations
points: Rule: If a given family of curves contains 'n' independent arbitrary constants, differentiate 'n' times to get 'n' equations, and eliminate all arbitrary constants.
The resulting differential equation will have order equal to 'n'.
Examples:
1. Family of circles with centre at origin (x² + y² = r²): 1 constant (r) ⟹ Order = 1 (x + y y' = 0).
2. Family of all lines y = mx + c: 2 constants (m, c) ⟹ Order = 2 (y'' = 0).
3. Family of parabolas y² = 4ax: 1 constant (a) ⟹ Order = 1 (2xy' = y).

formulas.label: Order vs Constants
formulas.expr: Order of D.E. = Number of arbitrary constants

nodes.title: Variable Separable Method
points: Form: f(x) dx + g(y) dy = 0 or dy/dx = f(x) · g(y).
Method: Separate terms containing x with dx and terms containing y with dy: (1/g(y)) dy = f(x) dx.
Integrate both sides: ∫ (1/g(y)) dy = ∫ f(x) dx + c.
Substitution for Reducible to Separable: dy/dx = f(ax + by + c).
Put u = ax + by + c ⟹ du/dx = a + b(dy/dx) ⟹ dy/dx = (1/b)(du/dx − a).
Separates as: [1 / (a + b f(u))] du = dx.

formulas.label: Reducible to separable
formulas.expr: Put u = ax + by + c ⟹ du/dx = a + b(dy/dx)

nodes.title: Homogeneous Differential Equations
points: Form: dy/dx = f(x, y) / g(x, y), where f and g are homogeneous functions of x and y of the same degree.
Test: f(kx, ky) = kⁿ f(x, y).
Solution Method:
Step 1: Substitute y = v x ⟹ dy/dx = v + x (dv/dx).
Step 2: Replace dy/dx and y to get: v + x (dv/dx) = F(v).
Step 3: Separate variables: [1 / (F(v) − v)] dv = (1/x) dx.
Step 4: Integrate both sides, then replace v = y/x.

nodes.title: First Order Linear Differential Equations (LDE)
points: Type 1: dy/dx + P(x) y = Q(x) (where P and Q are functions of x only or constants).
Integrating Factor (I.F.): I.F. = e^(∫ P dx).
General Solution: y · (I.F.) = ∫ [Q · (I.F.)] dx + c.
Type 2 (Interchanged variables): dx/dy + P(y) x = Q(y).
Integrating Factor: I.F. = e^(∫ P dy).
General Solution: x · (I.F.) = ∫ [Q · (I.F.)] dy + c.

nodes.title: General vs Particular Solutions
points: General Solution: Solution containing arbitrary constants equal to the order of the differential equation.
Particular Solution: Solution obtained by assigning specific values to the arbitrary constants using given initial conditions (e.g., y = y₀ when x = x₀).
A particular solution contains NO arbitrary constants.

formulas.label: Particular solution
formulas.expr: Evaluate c using initial condition (x₀, y₀)

nodes.title: Applications: Population, Decay & Newton's Cooling
points: Population Growth / Bacterial Growth: Rate of growth is proportional to current population N: dN/dt = k N ⟹ N(t) = N₀ e^(kt).
Radioactive Decay: Rate of disintegration is proportional to amount N present: dN/dt = −k N ⟹ N(t) = N₀ e^(−kt).
Newton's Law of Cooling: Rate of cooling is proportional to temperature excess over surroundings: dθ/dt = −k(θ − θ₀) ⟹ θ − θ₀ = C e^(−kt), where θ₀ is ambient temperature.

formulas.label: Newton's cooling law
formulas.expr: dθ/dt = −k(θ − θ₀) ⟹ θ − θ₀ = C e^(−kt)

nodes.title: Geometric Applications of Differential Equations
points: Slope of tangent at (x, y): dy/dx.
Slope of normal at (x, y): −dx/dy.
Length of Tangent: y √(1 + (dx/dy)²). Length of Subtangent: |y / (dy/dx)|.
Length of Normal: y √(1 + (dy/dx)²). Length of Subnormal: |y (dy/dx)|.
Finding equation of curve passing through given point with specified slope condition.

nodes.title: Must-Know Board Theorems & Questions
points: Board Favourite #1: Solve homogeneous differential equation: x² y dx − (x³ + y³) dy = 0.
Board Favourite #2: Solve linear differential equation: dy/dx + y sec x = tan x.
Board Favourite #3: Solve differential equation by substitution: dy/dx = (4x + y + 1)².
Board Favourite #4: Word Problem: The population of a town grows at a rate proportional to its current population. If it doubles in 20 years, in how many years will it triple?
Board Favourite #5: Word Problem: A body cools from 80 °C to 60 °C in 20 minutes when room temperature is 20 °C. Find temperature after further 20 minutes.

formulas.label: LDE step
formulas.expr: I.F. = e^(∫ sec x dx) = sec x + tan x

nodes.title: MHT-CET Shortcuts, I.F. Hacks & Degree Traps
points: Integrating Factor Simplification Hacks:
2. e^(n ln x) = xⁿ.
4. e^(2 ln(sec x)) = sec²x.
Degree Trap: In e^(dy/dx) + d²y/dx² = x, Order = 2, but Degree is NOT DEFINED!
Order from Constants: Differential equation of all circles touching X-axis at origin: (x² + (y − r)² = r²) has 1 parameter (r) ⟹ Order = 1.
Differential equation of all parabolas having axis of symmetry along X-axis: (y² = 4a(x − h)) has 2 parameters (a, h) ⟹ Order = 2.
